application.name: ofetch
application.summary: The core is `createFetch` (src/fetch.ts): a factory that builds a `$fetch` callable with `.raw`, `.native`, and `.create` methods. Requests are prepared (options, headers, query, body serialization), executed with optional timeout/abort, responses are parsed by detected content type, and failures flow through a retry policy into normalized FetchError throws. Utilities in src/utils.ts handle option merging, hook invocation, body serialization checks, and response-type detection. src/error.ts builds the rich FetchError. src/node.ts adapts fetch for Node with optional keep-alive agents.
application.purpose: A universal TypeScript fetch client library. It exports `ofetch`/`$fetch`, an enhanced wrapper around the standard fetch API that adds automatic JSON serialization/parsing, retry and timeout handling, normalized errors (FetchError), lifecycle hooks, baseURL/query support, and typed responses. It ships a universal entry (browser/global runtime) and a Node.js-specific entry.

terminology.meaning: The library's fetch instance created by createFetch; callable directly, with `.raw` (full response), `.native` (pass-through fetch), and `.create` (instance with default options).
Normalized error type carrying request, options, response, parsed body (`data`), and status/statusCode/statusText.
Per-request context object (request, options, response, error) passed through hooks and error creation.
User callbacks: onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError (single function or array).
Retry behavior options: number of retries, delay (fixed or callback), and status codes eligible for retry.
Request timeout in milliseconds, implemented via AbortController producing a TimeoutError.
Base URL prefixing and query-parameter merging/serialization onto string requests.
Desired parsed response shape: json (default), text, blob, arrayBuffer, or stream.
Custom response parsing function overriding default parsing (destr-based JSON parsing).
Options to always resolve successfully on HTTP error statuses (ignoreResponseError) instead of throwing.
Body-carrying HTTP methods: PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Central library factory. Produces the public fetch client ('ofetch'/'$fetch'), wires in fetch/Headers/AbortController, and orchestrates the full request lifecycle: option resolution, hook calls, body serialization, timeout, response parsing, and error/retry. Its self-call supports `$fetch.create(...)` for instances with merged defaults.

Failure handler implementing the retry policy: retries on configured status codes (default 408/409/425/429/500/502/503/504) with optional delay; skips retry for active aborts; otherwise throws a normalized FetchError.
Builds the library's normalized FetchError, exposing request, options, response, parsed `data`, and status/statusCode/statusText accessors from the fetch context.
Identifies body-carrying HTTP methods (PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE); drives body serialization behavior and the default retry count (0 for payload methods).
Decides whether a request body should be auto-JSON-stringified (plain objects, arrays, primitives; excludes FormData, URLSearchParams, binary buffers).
Maps a response Content-Type header to a parser: json (default), text, stream (for text/event-stream), or blob.
Combines per-call options with library defaults, merging headers and query/params into a single resolved options object per request.
Internal helper that merges default and per-request header collections into one Headers instance (request headers win).
Executes user lifecycle hooks (single or arrays) with the fetch context; powers onRequest/onRequestError/onResponse/onResponseError behavior.
Node.js adapter: returns native fetch when available, otherwise node-fetch-native; enables HTTP/HTTPS keep-alive agents when the FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment flag is true.
Example demonstrating the library's headline value: fetching repo metadata from ungh.cc and consuming a strongly typed JSON response.
Developer playground script exercising error behavior by calling a 500-returning endpoint (httpstat.us) with $fetch.
Test helper for the abort-with-retry scenario: aborts a request via AbortController signal and asserts the request rejects without retrying.
